note: Ground truth: 5 items (dis1..dis5), resp 1-6. TEXT/MAPPING: the S1 File .sav (10.1371/journal.pone.0208438.s001, CC BY 4.0) labels every column -- dis1 'been a very nervous person?', dis2 'felt peaceful and calm?', dis3 'felt downhearted and blue?', dis4 'been a happy person?', dis5 'felt so down in the dumps that nothing could cheer you up?' -- and item_text is those five labels transcribed character for character, including the trailing question marks and dis2's 'peaceful and calm' word order (the canonical MHI/SF-36 reads 'calm and peaceful'; not normalised). CODE DERIVATION: data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts the .sav on the literal column list [f'dis{i}' for i in range(1,6)], so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- derivation pattern 1, no positional assignment and no rename, hence Step 5b exempt (data_labels) and no verify_<table>.R. STEP 3b: passes. The paper's Measures section says 'We measured psychological distress using five items selected from the Mental Health Inventory [48]' (Veit & Ware 1983); the five labelled dis* columns are exactly the MHI-5 (nervous / calm and peaceful / downhearted and blue / happy / down in the dumps), 5 items and a 6-point scale as the live table has, and the .sav's other scales sit under their own prefixes (pcl*, trait*, need*, ost*, msp*), so 'distress' names the right instrument. SCALE DIRECTION, checked against the data rather than assumed (N=127-128 in the .sav): the file ships precomputed reverse columns dis1R/dis3R/dis5R and each equals 7 - dis_i exactly (max |diff| = 0 over 127 cases); the file's own composite 'distress' ('mental distress average') equals mean(dis1R, dis2, dis3R, dis4, dis5R) exactly (max |diff| = 0, N=128) while the raw five-item mean is off by up to 3.00; and that composite correlates +0.732 with the file's ptsd average, +0.757 with traitanx, +0.703 with stateanx and -0.532 with support, so higher = more distress. It follows that a LOW raw value on the negatively-worded items means MORE distress, i.e. 1 = All of the time and 6 = Never, exactly as the paper states. Raw means agree: dis4 'been a happy person' 2.64 (frequent end) vs dis5 'down in the dumps' 5.07 (Never end). Polarity classes also match the labels: dis1/dis3/dis5 intercorrelate +0.677..+0.780 and correlate -0.600..-0.737 with dis2/dis4, which are +0.841 with each other. DEVIATIONS: option_text populated only at resp=1 ('All of the time') and resp=6 ('Never'), both quoted from the paper; resp=2..5 left blank because the .sav has no value labels (empty variable_value_labels) and the paper prints no middle anchors -- scale points were NOT padded with their own numbers or with canonical MHI anchors. The instructions field 'How much of the time during the past month have you...' is the canonical MHI/SF-36 item stem, supplied because the shipped item_text values are sentence fragments; the paper corroborates the past-month window and the frequency format but does not reproduce the stem, so that one field is not this study's wording. RIGHTS: no block. The wording was copied from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit, and the originator is RAND Health Care, whose Mental Health Inventory Survey page states under Permissions Information: "All of the surveys from RAND Health Care are public documents, available without charge." (https://www.rand.org/health-care/surveys_tools/mos/mental-health.html, read 2026-09-16 via web.archive.org/web/2024/, page sha256 b30de3af6178bd2d4a9384e05f08ba847b916bae7fb11ae2249e001204bdc25b) -- nothing reserved: no fee, no permission-required, no non-commercial, no no-derivatives, no no-redistribution. instrument_rights_register.csv already carries a ratified-pending verdict=ship row for the RAND 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36 v1, row added 2026-09-09 batch_121) under the same RAND clause template, and these five items are that survey's mental-health subscale, so the existing row was APPLIED, not re-derived. No register row was written by this round: a round may write block rows only, and the MHI would be a ship row -- flagged here for Ben's ratification if it is worth banking as its own instrument row.
